Key Research Thinking Patterns: Explicit Resolution Construction: Building concrete algebraic structures to compute cohomology, exemplified by the three-step partial resolution and double complex of resolutions for Steinberg modules.

Connectivity via Combinatorial Topology: Proving homological vanishing and stability by analyzing the topological connectivity of simplicial complexes, such as the double Tits building and common basis complexes.

Axiomatic Homological Stability: Extending stability results to twisted coefficients by establishing general axiomatic frameworks that propagate stability across group families like mapping class and symplectic groups.

Monoid Homology and Koszul Duality: Investigating the algebraic structure of equivariant rings by proving the Koszulity of the Steinberg monoid through lexicographic filtrations and contracting homotopies on reduced bar complexes.
Summary Description: Peter Patzt specializes in algebraic topology and geometric group theory, focusing on the cohomology of arithmetic groups and algebraic K-theory. His research bridges abstract homological algebra with number theory, utilizing explicit resolution constructions and connectivity analyses of Tits buildings to verify major conjectures, including Rognes' connectivity conjecture and the Church-Farb-Putman conjecture. Patzt employs axiomatic frameworks to establish homological stability for twisted coefficients across diverse group families. Recently, he has expanded into monoid homology, proving the Koszulity of the Steinberg monoid via bar complex filtrations. His work provides foundational tools for understanding stable real cohomology, integral vanishing phenomena, and statistical properties of L-functions over function fields.
